name: Reconcile Cluster
description: Top-level Reconcile loop: validates the spec and the image tag against the version the servers run (status.version) on every pass, refusing with phase Failed and a ValidationFailed event, provisions TLS/RBAC/Services/ConfigMap, applies the server StatefulSet (holding replicas during a scale-down drain, and keeping the partition a Paused or Failed upgrade left, also when a storage expansion creates the StatefulSet again), collects diagnostics once the cluster has formed, and marks the cluster Ready once formation and rollout are both verified (the servers a held upgrade keeps below its partition are not a rollout in flight, and status.message then names the held upgrade, operations.md id 149) (recording status.version from the rolled server StatefulSet when it differs: at the first Ready, and after an image the zero-ready escape hatch let through, but not while a Failed or Paused upgrade targets that tag — operations.md id 144), requeueing a Ready cluster after --ready-poll-interval (default 30s; every other path keeps RequeueAfter) — or hands a cluster that is short of servers to the shortfall assessment. On deletion, it deletes the {name}-tls-secret cert-manager issued for its {name}-tls Certificate (#479), and releasing the finalizer withdraws the cluster's metric series. The server pods run under the {cluster}-discovery ServiceAccount, bound to no Role (LIST discovery never calls the Kubernetes API); a {cluster}-discovery Role, RoleBinding or Service (V1 port 5000) the cluster controls, created by releases up to v1.20, is deleted. A failed pass is retried on its own 5–30s backoff, with a shared 10/s storm guard. ApplyDefaults' defaults go on the pass's own copy and are never written back: the finalizer is added and released, and the scale-down and Aura fleet deployment annotations are set, as merge patches of what changed (with the object's resourceVersion), never as an Update, which wrote the defaults, a false the CRD defaults to true as true, and a quantity in its canonical spelling into the stored spec. The stored spec stays the one the user applied (operations.md id 150). A template write the StatefulSet controller has not observed (observedGeneration behind generation), or a cached read older than the generation the pass wrote, is a rollout in flight, so the pass does not report a stale Ready from its own write; status.observedGeneration and the conditions' observedGeneration are the generation the pass read and acted on. The Ready pass records, with the Ready status and only when they change, the versions the servers report for a tag without a patch (status.runningVersion; for a held upgrade status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion), read from the formation check's SHOW SERVERS (operations.md id 153). A refused spec (validation, server role hints, property sharding, a missing StorageClass) is logged at info on the pass that announces it and at V(1) on the passes in between, never as an ERROR on every pass (operations.md id 136). Every label that carries the image tag (app.kubernetes.io/version) carries it without a digest, cut to a valid label value, so a tag pinned to a digest no longer fails the ConfigMap write (#562 walk; id 149). A server StatefulSet a storage expansion deleted is created again as it was (Recreate StatefulSet As It Was, id 171). A deletion whose finalizer release finds the cluster already gone is done, logged at V(1), not an ERROR and a reconcile error (operations.md id 164).

name: Reconcile Cluster ConfigMap
description: Renders the cluster's {cluster}-config ConfigMap (neo4j.conf, startup.sh, health.sh) and decides whether the servers must restart. The restart decision compares a normalised rendering that drops full-line comments and blank lines and masks runtime-variable lines. When only neo4j.conf changed and every changed setting is dynamic (SHOW SETTINGS isDynamic), not set by an env var, and the cluster is Ready with every server up, it runs dbms.setConfigValue on every server first and restarts nothing (ConfigAppliedLive); otherwise it stamps config-restart on the server StatefulSet, rolling every server (ConfigNeedsRestart says why). The ConfigMap is written whenever its raw content changes, after any live apply, so a later restart keeps the values. Startup-script lines between the restart-neutral markers (the system database role block, which makes servers past minSystemPrimaries system secondaries at their first start and records the role on their volume) never count; a change confined to the membership lines (TOTAL_SERVERS, the discovery endpoint list) restarts nothing unless a scale-up adds a system primary (ScaledWithoutRestart). It records on the ConfigMap which settings it applies at the next restart and since when (neo4j.com/deferred-settings, neo4j.com/deferred-settings-since). When spec.monitoring.logs.stdout lists a log, it also renders server-logs.xml (Neo4j's default file appenders for the line plus a JSON Console appender per listed log) and adds server.logs.config=/operator-conf/server-logs.xml; the restart hash never covers server-logs.xml, so a changed list reloads through the mount without a restart. neo4j.conf sets dbms.cluster.network.connect_timeout=5s (Neo4j's default is 30s) unless spec.config sets it: a replaced pod's old IP can stay in the other servers' DNS cache for up to 30s, and a connection to it waits out the whole timeout.

name: Reconcile RestartPending
description: Maintains the RestartPending condition for settings the operator applies at each server's next restart instead of restarting for them. Two kinds: startup-script settings written by the restart-neutral block (dbms.cluster.raft.async_channel_acquisition_enabled on 5.26.29+, dbms.security.tls_reload_enabled on CalVer 2025.03+ with cert-manager TLS), and live changes of restart-effective dynamic settings that a live apply changes only in part (dbms.cluster.network.connect_timeout: Raft connections take it up only at a restart). The two have separate records on the cluster ConfigMap: neo4j.com/deferred-settings(-since) for the startup-script settings, and neo4j.com/restart-effective-settings(-since), stamped by ReconcileConfigMap only when a write changes such a setting's value against the running ConfigMap (an added line on upgrade from v1.20.x, or a spec.config edit; an unchanged value or a new ConfigMap records nothing). A server is waiting for a setting when its Neo4j has it (dbms.components() per pod, only for a version-gated setting) and its neo4j container started before that setting's record. With neither record the condition is absent. SHOW SETTINGS is not used: on 5.26.31 it misreports the async Raft setting, and it reports a live-applied value the Raft connections do not use yet. Best-effort; re-reads only when the pods or the settings change. Its per-server connection (dialClusterPod, shared with live config changes and TLS reloads) reads the admin Secret the servers were given, spec.auth.adminSecret or the default neo4j-admin-secret when it is unset; it used to refuse a cluster without the field (operations.md id 132).

name: Reload Renewed TLS Certificate
description: When {name}-tls-secret (owned by cert-manager, watched by name) holds a certificate the servers do not present, reads dbms.security.tls_reload_enabled on each ready server and, where it is true, runs dbms.security.reloadTLS() and confirms the certificate a new TLS connection gets (the procedure also succeeds, doing nothing, when reload is disabled). Retries while the kubelet projects the files (throttled to 30s, up to 10 minutes after the certificate's NotBefore), reports servers that must restart instead, and records the fingerprint on the StatefulSet (neo4j.com/tls-certificate). Shared by the cluster and standalone reconcilers; CalVer 2025.03+ with cert-manager TLS only.

name: Reconcile OpenShift Route
description: Creates or updates the OpenShift Route of a cluster or standalone (spec.service.route: {name}-client-route or {name}-route) and of its MCP server ({name}-mcp-route), shared by both reconcilers (reconcileRoute, reconcileMCPRoute). The mutate step (applyDesiredRoute) writes what the operator renders — labels, annotations, spec.to, spec.port, spec.path, spec.host when the user names one, and spec.tls termination and insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy — and keeps the rest: the wildcardPolicy and generated host (with its openshift.io/host.generated annotation) OpenShift's API server fills in, and a certificate added to the Route by hand, so a Route that is already right is not written again (#536). tls.secretName is not rendered and raises a ValidationWarning. Without the Route API it skips the Route and raises an advisory RouteAPINotFound (knowledge operations.md ids 102, 145, 148).

name: Merge Fleet Management Plugin
description: Phase 1 of Aura Fleet Management, for a cluster or standalone with spec.auraFleetManagement.enabled: addFleetManagementPlugin merges fleet-management into the neo4j container's NEO4J_PLUGINS with MergeNeo4jPluginList. It runs in the write that creates the StatefulSet — after the record of the env the deployment owns, so NEO4J_PLUGINS stays out of the static template and out of that record — so a new deployment's servers start with the plugin; and on every pass as mergeFleetManagementPlugin, which writes only when the entry is missing (enabling it on a running deployment restarts the servers once). A StatefulSet that does not exist yet is not a failure; anything else raises AuraFleetManagementPluginPatchFailed (knowledge operations.md ids 164, 175).

name: Reconcile Standalone
description: Top-level standalone reconcile: validates the spec on every pass with StandaloneValidator.Validate (the spec rules, the admin-secret password shape, and spec.image.tag against status.version: a downgrade turns it Failed with a ValidationFailed event and leaves the pod on the version it runs), reconciles TLS/ConfigMap/Service/StatefulSet/Ingress, runs a pre-upgrade health check and announces UpgradeStarted on the pass that applies a new image (the StatefulSet's template does not carry it yet), and updates status once the StatefulSet reports one ready replica. status.version is the image tag of a StatefulSet whose pod is ready on the current template, never spec.image.tag. Both upgrade strategies give the StatefulSet RollingUpdate, which replaces the one pod; Recreate used to select OnDelete, under which a new image, config or plugin never reached the server (operations.md id 144). A Ready standalone requeues after --ready-poll-interval (default 30s); otherwise RequeueAfter. With spec.podServiceAccountAnnotations it creates the `<name>-neo4j` ServiceAccount before the StatefulSet and runs the pod under it, and deletes it once the field is removed and no pod uses it. The pod template carries a hash of the raw neo4j.conf, so a changed conf restarts the pod; a change only in comments or blank lines keeps the running pod's hash (the normalised conf hash is recorded on the StatefulSet) and restarts nothing. A neo4j.conf change of dynamic settings only is applied to the running pod with dbms.setConfigValue before the conf is written, and the pod keeps its hash. With cert-manager TLS on CalVer 2025.03+, its conf enables TLS reload (applied at the next restart, ignored by the restart decision) and a renewed certificate is reloaded on the running pod. On deletion it deletes the {name}-tls-secret cert-manager issued for its {name}-tls-cert Certificate (#479). With spec.monitoring.logs.stdout it writes server-logs.xml into its ConfigMap (deleting it when no log is listed) and points server.logs.config at /conf/server-logs.xml, so Neo4j's listed logs reach standard output as JSON. The finalizer is added and released, and the Aura fleet deployment annotation set, as merge patches of what changed, never as an Update, which wrote the spec back as the Go types encode it (an explicit monitoring.enabled: false came back true); the stored spec stays the one the user applied (operations.md id 150). For a status.version without a patch it records status.runningVersion, the version the server reports, with one SHOW SERVERS once Ready and again only when its container runs another image; updateStatus clears it when status.version moves (operations.md id 153). Its OpenShift Route is written once per pass at most, at the end of the Service step (a second, unconditional write later in the pass was removed, #536). status.observedGeneration and the Ready condition's are the generation the pass acted on, not the one its write re-reads (#550; operations.md id 153). Its status is Ready only when its pod is ready on the StatefulSet's latest pod template; while a template write rolls out it is Pending ("Waiting for the standalone to restart on its latest pod template: …"). A refused spec or a missing StorageClass is logged at info on the pass that announces it and at V(1) after, never as an ERROR on every pass (operations.md id 136). A StatefulSet a storage expansion deleted is created again as it was, so its pod is not replaced (id 171). A deletion whose finalizer release finds the standalone already gone is done, logged at V(1) (operations.md id 164). A StatefulSet a storage expansion deleted is created again in the same pass once the delete has gone through.

name: Merge Env Vars
description: Computes the StatefulSet container's next env-var list: applies the cluster controller's desired vars, drops names in the previously-owned annotation that are no longer desired, and preserves foreign vars added by plugin/fleet/Aura controllers.

name: Merge Init Containers and Volumes
description: On a template apply of the server StatefulSet, merges the pod template's init containers and volumes by name (mergeOwnedByName): applies what the cluster renders, drops what it rendered on its last apply (recorded in the neo4j.com/cluster-controller-init-containers and neo4j.com/cluster-controller-volumes StatefulSet annotations, written from the desired template) and no longer renders, and keeps the rest — a VerifiedDownload Neo4jPlugin's init container and its plugin-auth/plugin-ca volumes. The comparisons that decide whether a stable cluster's template changed leave those kept items out, so they never trigger an apply. A StatefulSet without the record (an earlier operator's) counts every init container as the cluster's except those listed in the plugin controller's neo4j.com/plugin-init-containers pod-template annotation, and every volume except those only such an init container mounts.

name: Collect Cluster Diagnostics
description: Runs SHOW SERVERS and SHOW DATABASES against a cluster that has formed — Ready, Degraded, or mid-rollout with ClusterFormed=True, so it keeps reporting while a server is down —, fills the address of a server that is down from the per-cluster address book (SHOW SERVERS reports none for it), and writes results plus ServersHealthy/DatabasesHealthy conditions into status.diagnostics; non-fatal — every error is surfaced only in status.diagnostics.collectionError, never returned to the caller. The result is written to status only when it changed (lists sorted; databases' transaction counters ignored) or lastCollected is 5 minutes old: a status write re-enqueues the reconcile, so writing every pass looped it (#475). A query that fails because a server could not be reached (a pod deleted or restarting, ConnectivityError: EOF) is logged at info; any other failure is logged as an error (#549; knowledge operations.md id 164). Neo4j answering "not now" — a Neo.TransientError.* (a database unavailable while it restarts or fails over), NotALeader — is logged at info like a server that cannot be reached (IsTransientError); a real error stays at error (knowledge operations.md id 164).

name: Collect Standalone Diagnostics
description: Runs SHOW DATABASES (plus users/roles) against a Ready standalone instance and writes status.diagnostics; non-fatal, mirroring the cluster path's collectionError-only error handling. The result is written to status only when it changed (lists sorted; databases' transaction counters ignored) or lastCollected is 5 minutes old: a status write re-enqueues the reconcile, so writing every pass looped it (#475). A query that fails because the server could not be reached is logged at info; any other failure as an error (#549). Neo4j answering "not now" — a Neo.TransientError.* (a database unavailable while it restarts or fails over), NotALeader — is logged at info like a server that cannot be reached (IsTransientError); a real error stays at error (knowledge operations.md id 164).

name: Collect Users And Roles
description: Runs SHOW USERS and SHOW ROLES, sorts and caps each result list at 50 rows, and appends any query failure to the shared collectionError string without aborting the rest of diagnostics collection (e.g. when the connecting user lacks SHOW USER/SHOW ROLE privilege).

name: Advance Rolling Upgrade
description: Dispatches exactly one non-blocking state-machine step per reconcile (Staging, Rolling, Stabilizing, Verifying) and re-stages from any active phase if the target image tag changes mid-flight (a new target below status.version, or below the current target once a server runs it, is refused by the validation that runs before it), so an in-flight upgrade never blocks reconciliation of other clusters. Each phase transition restarts status.upgradeStatus.phaseStartTime and records the ended phase's duration in neo4j_operator_upgrade_duration_seconds exactly once, derived from the persisted phaseStartTime. In Rolling it lowers the partition only after the server it just restarted is Available and every database copy on it has caught up (statusCheck APPLYING, SHOW DATABASES at requested status), naming the lagging databases in status.upgradeStatus.message (#488). The availability check reads the restarted server's SHOW SERVERS row, version included: for a target without a patch it records that version in status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion once the server is available (operations.md id 153). Completed writes status.version (the tag) with status.runningVersion, the highest version the servers reported to Verifying for a tag without a patch, cleared for one that names its patch. After each step, the pass collects the cluster's diagnostics (SHOW SERVERS, SHOW DATABASES → status.diagnostics, ServersHealthy, DatabasesHealthy, server_health) at most once per --ready-poll-interval, so they follow the servers through the upgrade; nothing else of the normal pass runs while an upgrade is active. Before an upgrade starts it checks the upgrade path with the same rule the validation runs (ValidateVersionUpgrade against status.version). Every image change on a Ready cluster goes through it, whatever spec.upgradeStrategy.strategy says: Recreate is accepted with a ValidationWarning and does what RollingUpgrade does (it used to return before the machine started, so a Ready cluster kept its old image and no other spec change was applied while the tag differed), and the server StatefulSet is always RollingUpdate, never OnDelete. A step's timeout is a Go duration above zero; one at or below zero is refused by validation, and the getters fall back to the default (operations.md id 144). A Paused or Failed upgrade taken up again keeps its start time and progress (operations.md id 149). An upgrade a scale-down drain holds back is announced (UpgradeDeferred) once per target, not on each 15s check (#527). Staging keeps the StatefulSet's replica count, whatever spec.topology.servers says, and freezes the partition at the lowest of the restarted servers that cannot start on the image they run, when the new template changes it, so the StatefulSet replaces them first (operations.md ids 162, 163). Rolling reports a topology change in either direction in the TopologyChangeDeferred condition. Starting, resuming or retargeting an upgrade on a cluster that is Ready with every server available writes its status.message: the upgrade is in progress (#553). Every Rolling pass, a retarget and a resumed held upgrade first record whether a restarted server's neo4j container has started on the target (status.upgradeStatus.startedTargetVersion); a retarget below what a server started on waits, re-checked against that record before it re-stages, since validation may have read it before the server started. On a formed cluster short of servers (the repair walk: Ready with Degraded, Degraded, or Forming) the walk's status.message says the upgrade is in progress and that the servers that could not start are replaced first, keeping the phase, instead of naming the server that was down when it began (#562 walk; operations.md id 149). Staging runs once per target: it reads the stored upgrade record and the StatefulSet uncached and does nothing when the record has moved on, and when the template already carries the target it keeps the live partition rather than raising it over servers on the target (a server being replaced came back on the current revision: an extra restart, or the unpullable held target after an expansion, #562 re-walk). It waits, writing the held template back itself, while a StatefulSet created again after an expansion has not got it back (operations.md ids 162, 171).

name: Pause Or Fail Rolling Upgrade
description: Routes a failed upgrade step to Paused (manual intervention required, never auto-resumed: the user changes spec.image.tag or turns autoPauseOnFailure off) when upgradeStrategy.autoPauseOnFailure is set, or to Failed so the operator retries the upgrade once the cluster is Ready with every server available. Either way the StatefulSet keeps the partition the step left, so no server the upgrade has not rolled restarts onto the target outside the state machine. An attempt refused before Staging records the target it was for. The phase that was active when the step failed is recorded in neo4j_operator_upgrade_duration_seconds (operations.md id 149). A refusal by a check before Staging goes through Refuse Upgrade Start instead, which leaves the cluster Ready. The stop is logged once at info when its record is written, with the Warning event; it is not an ERROR, and a Failed upgrade is requeued for the normal pass rather than returned as a reconcile error (#562 re-walk).

name: Hold A Stopped Upgrade
description: While an upgrade is Paused or Failed (upgradeHeld), keeps the server StatefulSet's RollingUpdate partition where the state machine left it: every normal-path apply keeps the live partition, and a StatefulSet created again (storage expansion) starts at status.upgradeStatus.currentPartition, or frozen at replicas if nothing was staged. The servers below it are not a rollout in flight, so the cluster can be Ready (or a server short) while its servers run two versions, and users, roles, databases and backups keep working. Only the state machine moves the partition: a Failed upgrade is retried once every server is available; a Paused one waits while upgradeWaitsForUser (autoPauseOnFailure set and spec.image.tag the record's target) (internal/controller/upgrade_hold.go, operations.md id 149). For a target without a patch, the held cluster's next Ready pass records what the servers at or above the partition report in status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion, so a tag below it is refused even when the upgrade paused before its availability check saw the restarted server (operations.md id 153). While it keeps a partition, a change of spec.topology.servers waits (Hold Topology During Upgrade, operations.md id 163). While it holds, each normal pass records whether a server has started on the target (an image may have become pullable), and drops the record of a held upgrade no server started on whose target spec.image.tag no longer names and whose target the StatefulSet's template does not carry, so its 'takes it up again' message goes (#562 walk; operations.md id 149).

name: Verify Version Upgrade
description: Confirms every Enabled server in SHOW SERVERS reports the target image version, applying a kernel-alias normalization for the one CalVer release (2025.01.x) that self-reports as kernel 5.27.x, before the upgrade is allowed to complete. The patch is compared only when the tag names one: a patch-less tag (5.26-enterprise, 2026.08-enterprise) floats to the newest patch of its line, so any patch of that line passes (operations.md id 149). On success it returns the highest version the Enabled servers reported, which the Completed write records as status.runningVersion for a tag without a patch (operations.md id 153).

name: Detect Split Brain
description: Queries each running server pod's own SHOW SERVERS view, groups pods that see similar cluster configurations, and flags a split-brain when a minority group's servers are not a subset of the majority group's visible servers. Runs only on a cluster that has been healthy: phase Ready or Degraded. On a Ready cluster whose server pods have not changed it runs at most every --split-brain-check-interval (default 5m; 0 runs it every pass), as decided by Verify Cluster Formation. Its per-server clients read the admin Secret the servers were given, spec.auth.adminSecret or the default neo4j-admin-secret when it is unset (getClusterAdminSecretName); they used to refuse a cluster without the field, as did the upgrade's per-server database gate, which uses the same client (operations.md id 132).

name: Restart Orphaned Pods
description: Repairs a detected split-brain by deleting the orphaned pods (or, in the nuclear-option repair action, every server pod) so the StatefulSet recreates them and they rejoin the majority cluster view.

name: Drain Server For Scale-Down
description: Drives one cordon/deallocate/wait/drop step per reconcile for servers being removed by a topology scale-down, gating on a DEALLOCATE dry-run and the system database's minimum-voting-member floor before ever cordoning a server. Each step is decided from SHOW SERVERS read on the system leader (a follower's view can lag), and a refusal saying a server is already deallocating or dropped is treated as progress, not a block (#476). The draining-servers annotation on the cluster is written as a merge patch of that annotation alone (operations.md id 150).

name: Plan Scale-Down Step
description: Pure decision function that inspects the live State/Hosting of each drain-target server and picks the single next drain action (cordon, deallocate, wait, or drop) for the caller to execute — a draining server hosting only `system` is droppable even if stuck in Deallocating.

name: Expand Cluster Storage
description: Compares each server-StatefulSet PVC's current size against spec.storage.size, rejects any shrink attempt, and on growth patches the PVCs then orphan-deletes the StatefulSet so it is recreated with the updated VolumeClaimTemplates.

name: Expand Standalone Storage
description: Standalone twin of sf-expand-storage: compares the neo4j-data PVC size against spec.storage.size, rejects shrinks, and patches plus orphan-deletes the single-replica StatefulSet on growth so it is recreated with the enlarged claim template.

name: Check Storage Expansion Needed
description: Compares desired PVC storage size from spec.storage.size against the live PVCs' storage requests and reports match, expand, or shrink so the caller can decide whether to proceed, no-op, or hard-reject.

name: Calculate Topology Placement
description: Determines whether topology-spread and/or anti-affinity should be applied, auto-discovers availability zones from cluster-scoped Nodes when none are configured, and degrades to best-effort zone spread (rather than failing) when node listing is unavailable in namespace-scoped installs. The TopologyPlacementCalculated event is announced when the zones change, not on every pass (#527).

name: Apply Topology Constraints
description: Applies the calculated topology-spread constraints and/or pod anti-affinity rules onto the server StatefulSet's pod template before it is created or updated.

name: Verify Cluster Formation
description: Checks Bolt connectivity (tracking a consecutive-failure streak for outage forensics), then runs split-brain detection with a legacy SHOW SERVERS count fallback to decide whether the cluster has formed with the expected number of Enabled+Available servers. On a Ready cluster the full split-brain check is skipped, and the cluster counted formed from SHOW SERVERS through the client Service, when that lists every expected server Enabled and Available and a full check found the cluster whole within --split-brain-check-interval (default 5m) against the same server pods: none deleted, recreated, restarted or changed readiness since. Only such a clean check is recorded (in memory, per cluster); any other outcome clears the record, so the next pass checks in full. Returns the SHOW SERVERS list it saw and whether the shortfall is a split-brain, for the shortfall assessment. Its SHOW SERVERS yields each server's version too, which the Ready pass records for a tag without a patch (status.runningVersion, status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion while an upgrade is held) without a query of its own (operations.md id 153). It has no error to return: every way the check comes back short — no connection, no server list, a split-brain — is a formationCheck the shortfall assessment reads (the ClusterFormationFailed branch it fed could never run, #531).

name: Hold Image Drift Until Ready
description: While the cluster is not Ready, pins the in-memory spec image back to whatever the live StatefulSet currently runs so the normal reconcile path can't apply a version change outside the upgrade state machine, unless zero replicas are ready (nothing to protect: a first deploy wedged on a bad tag, or a cluster that has lost every server). The tag has already been checked against status.version, and the Ready pass records the new version once every server runs it (operations.md id 144). The image in place is the server StatefulSet's, or, while a storage expansion has orphan-deleted it, the image the highest-ordinal orphaned server pod runs, so the StatefulSet created again does not roll every server onto the held image ungated (#538). The image is split as the operator built it: a tag may carry a digest (#531). Its UpgradeDeferred is announced on the second pass that holds the same image, once, and not for a change a stopped upgrade's record already names (#550).

name: Is Upgrade Required
description: Detects image drift on the server StatefulSet (or a Failed upgrade, or a Paused one whose autoPauseOnFailure has been turned off, whose target is still spec.image.tag while status.version disagrees) to decide whether a rolling upgrade should start or be taken up again; never fires while a Paused upgrade still waits for the user (autoPauseOnFailure set and the tag unchanged), already mid-flight, or while a server is unavailable (Degraded condition True), since rolling the others could cost the cluster its majority (operations.md id 149). Exception: a held upgrade whose restarted servers cannot start on its target, with spec.image.tag moved to another image, is taken up although servers are down (operations.md id 162). An attempt at the same image a check refused before Staging is tried again only once a minute has passed, so the normal pass runs in between (id 149).

name: Ensure Seed Credentials Projected
description: Validates that a hosting cluster or standalone CR's spec.extraEnvFrom projects the cloud-credentials Secret a seedURI restore needs, auto-patching it in (and triggering a rolling restart) only when the CR carries the neo4j.com/auto-inherit-seed-creds annotation. The entry and the neo4j.com/seed-creds-auto-inherited-from annotation are written as a merge patch, never an Update, so nothing else in the user's spec changes (operations.md id 150).

name: Ensure PVC Seed Proxy
description: Idempotently creates the busybox-httpd Deployment, Service, and NetworkPolicy that expose a backup PVC over HTTP so Neo4j's URLConnectionSeedProvider can seed a database from it during a restore; the policy admits only the target's server pods (a cluster's neo4j.com/cluster label, a standalone's app label). The provider fetches one file, so a differential's chain is merged first (sf-merge-seed-chain).

name: Merge PVC Backup Chain for Seeding
description: newSeedMergePlan / applySeedMerge (pvc_seed_merge.go): when a PVC seed artifact is not recorded as a FULL backup, the seed proxy pod gets a merge-chain init container running the target's Neo4j image that copies the chain to scratch space (emptyDir or spec.options.tempStorage), merges it with neo4j-admin database aggregate-backup (5.x) / backup aggregate (CalVer), and publishes the merged full artifact at the original relative path; a failed merge fails the restore at once with neo4j-admin's reason (rule 109). The merged result is checked with backup inspect --show-metadata and refused if it is a differential (5.26 reports an empty differential with no full as an existing full backup).

name: Reconcile Neo4jDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec inline, resolves the target host, checks readiness, projects seed credentials if needed, and ensures the database exists. A host that is missing, or that lacks the seed credentials Secret, is phase Pending; ClusterNotFound, SeedCredsMissing, CreationFailed and DataImportFailed are emitted only when the status write that records them changed something (knowledge operations.md id 145). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned spec.ifNotExists and spec.wait: false into true (operations.md id 150).

name: Create Or Verify Database
description: ensureDatabase() checks DatabaseExists, which matches the name ignoring case (neo4j.FindDatabase; Neo4j lists database names lower-cased, knowledge operations.md id 146), then issues CREATE DATABASE (plain, with TOPOLOGY, or from seedURI/seedURIs via OPTIONS) and reads the database out of SHOW DATABASES (observeDatabase): state folded over every copy (online when all are, otherwise the first other status by name) and the sorted server addresses, independent of row order and matching the name ignoring case. It returns that observation for the status write instead of setting it on the in-memory CR, which the write's re-fetch discarded (knowledge operations.md id 143). resolveDatabaseCreateInputs() decides the host-dependent inputs once for every create path: spec.defaultCypherLanguage is sent as DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER only when the target image is CalVer (neo4j.DefaultLanguageForImage; the 5.26 LTS has no such clause, so it is omitted), and spec.topology is ignored for a standalone host. All four create methods render through one statement builder.

name: Alter Database Topology
description: internal/neo4j/client.go's AlterDatabaseTopology issues ALTER DATABASE `name` SET TOPOLOGY n PRIMARIES m SECONDARIES for a post-bootstrap topology change; a capability of the Neo4j client, not currently auto-invoked from the Neo4jDatabase reconcile loop (CLAUDE.md documents it as an operator-triggered change).

name: Drop Database On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() resolves the host and issues DROP DATABASE for spec.name, releasing the finalizer on success or on a non-retryable failure. A retryable failure keeps the finalizer and requeues: the failure is written through updateDatabaseStatus (phase Error, Ready reason DeletionFailed) and DeletionFailed is emitted only when that write changed the status, once per failure rather than on every retry (knowledge operations.md id 145). After a successful drop it lists Neo4jRoles on the same clusterRef and warns (non-fatally) on each role whose spec still grants on the dropped database, case-insensitively.

name: Import Initial Data
description: importInitialData() executes each spec.initialData.cypherStatements entry against the new database once, skipped when the database was created from a seedURI.

name: Update Neo4jDatabase Status
description: updateDatabaseStatus() / updateDatabaseStatusObserved() re-fetch the CR under retry.RetryOnConflict and set the Ready condition, status.phase and status.message, plus the pass's SHOW DATABASES observation (status.state, status.servers) applied to the re-fetched object. Nothing is written when the status would not change (a status write is a watch event). They report whether the Ready condition's status or reason, the phase or the message changed, from the attempt whose write succeeded; reportDatabaseReady emits DatabaseReady and the validation gate emits ValidationFailed only on that transition (knowledge operations.md ids 136, 143). The phase follows the Ready reason: ValidationFailed is written as the api/v1beta1 constant PhaseValidationFailed, and DeletionFailed (a retried drop during deletion) as Error.

name: Reconcile Neo4jDatabaseAlias
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec inline, resolves clusterRef, waits for the target database to exist, then compares the live alias (if any) against spec.targetDatabase. Database and alias names are matched ignoring case, as Neo4j stores them lower-cased (knowledge operations.md id 146). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it (operations.md id 150).

name: Create Alias
description: Issues CREATE ALIAS when ShowAlias, which matches the name ignoring case, reports no existing alias with this name, pinned to Cypher 5 so the server's default language cannot change how a dotted name is read.

name: Retarget Alias
description: Issues ALTER ALIAS ... SET TARGET when the live alias's database differs from spec.targetDatabase, compared ignoring case (aliasTargetDiffers; drift correction; spec wins).

name: Drop Alias On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() issues DROP ALIAS IF EXISTS unless spec.deletionPolicy=Retain; a failed drop releases the finalizer rather than wedging deletion.

name: Reconcile Neo4jShardedDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves the referenced cluster, checks property-sharding readiness, opens a Neo4j client, and drives seed resolution plus create/status refresh. shardCreateNeeded decides whether CREATE DATABASE is sent: always on the destructive replaceExisting pass and while the readiness SHOW DATABASES lists no family (the virtual database and its -g000 graph shard); for a listed family only under ifNotExists: false when this CR did not create it (status.virtualDatabase does not name spec.name), so Neo4j's 'already exists' refusal surfaces instead of the family being adopted. ShardedDatabaseReady, SeedBackupPending, SeedProxyStarting and ValidationFailed are emitted only when the status write (transitionStatus) changes the phase or message. A clusterRef that names no cluster is phase Pending (ev-cluster-not-found, once), with the operator's validator wired in too: the validator reports the missing cluster as Pending, not as an error (#532); any other read error is retried with backoff. Every Warning about a lasting condition (cluster without property sharding, client creation, seedBackupRef resolution, a failed reconcile) is emitted only when the status write that records it changed the phase or message (knowledge operations.md id 145). Each pass reads the CR through the uncached APIReader (reader()), so the phase steps, shardedSeedConsumable and the destructive-restore generation guard decide from the last pass's write rather than a stale cache copy (knowledge operations.md ids 94, 136). A refused spec reads "Validation failed" once, in status and in the ValidationFailed event. transitionStatus copies the status its write stored into the pass's own copy, so a new CR's first pass writes Validating, Creating, then Ready (or the wait it meets); from its own copy it kept no phase after writing Validating and never wrote Creating (#549). From a Ready status an earlier operator left, the first pass writes and announces nothing (#553; knowledge operations.md id 136).

name: Create Sharded Database
description: createShardedDatabase() executes the statement buildCreateShardedDatabaseCypher() renders: `CYPHER 25 CREATE DATABASE ... SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 25 SET GRAPH SHARD {...} SET PROPERTY SHARDS {...} OPTIONS {...}`, binding every seed/user-supplied value as a driver parameter. The language clause is always emitted: shard sub-databases inherit the parent's language, and the server no longer forces CYPHER_25 for sharding. Called on the destructive replaceExisting pass, while SHOW DATABASES does not list the family, or under ifNotExists: false for a family this CR did not create: without IF NOT EXISTS Neo4j refuses CREATE on an existing name, which is what ifNotExists: false asks for. The keys of a per-shard seedURI map (spec.seedURIs, or the map resolved from seedBackupRef) are sent lower-cased, as Neo4j names the shards.

name: Drop Sharded Database For Replace
description: dropShardedDatabaseIfExists() issues `CYPHER 25 DROP DATABASE ... IF EXISTS DESTROY DATA WAIT`, gated to the spec.replaceExisting+force path and guarded by status.lastDestructiveRestoreGeneration so it never re-fires at the same generation.

name: Stamp Server Default Cypher Language
description: stampClusterCypherLanguage()/stampStandaloneCypherLanguage() resolve spec.serverDefaultCypherLanguage (resources.StampServerCypherLanguage) from the spec, a legacy db.query.default_language key, the existing stamp, the image line, whether the StatefulSet exists and the value in the current ConfigMap, and persist it to status.effectiveCypherLanguage before the ConfigMap that renders it is built (internal/controller/server_cypher_language.go).

name: Resolve And Serve Sharded Seed
description: resolveShardedSeed()/resolvePVCShardedSeed() turn spec.seedBackupRef into either per-shard cloud seedURIs or an operator-managed PVC seed-proxy Deployment+Service serving each shard's .backup file over HTTP. A PVC run with a shard recorded as DIFF is refused before the proxy starts (Neo4j seeds a sharded database over HTTP only from full backups, and merging drops the sharding header); the requeue seeds once a full run lands. For a cloud seed, ensureClusterSeedConfig() projects the backup's credentials and custom endpoint onto the cluster under the auto-inherit annotation and waits for the rollout. Without the annotation the database waits in phase Pending with one ev-seed-creds-missing, naming what is missing, and seeds once the cluster has it (knowledge operations.md id 145). The per-shard seedURI keys it builds, cloud and PVC, are the target's shard names lower-cased (shardSeedKey): Neo4j derives the shard names from the lower-cased database name and matches the keys exactly, so keys built from a capitalised spec.name were refused (knowledge operations.md id 146).

name: Update Shard Status
description: updateShardStatus() reads SHOW DATABASES once per reconcile and records, from those rows only, status.graphShard (`{name}-g000`), status.propertyShards (`{name}-pNNN`, ordered by index), status.virtualDatabase (the logical database) and status.creationTime (set once when the graph shard is first seen; restarted by a destructive recreate). Per-shard state is online only when every copy is online; ready means at least one copy is online and none that should be online is not. The write is skipped when nothing changed and failures are non-fatal. Shard size, servers, lastError, propertyCount, the virtual database's endpoint and metrics, and status.totalSize stay unpopulated because SHOW DATABASES does not carry them. Family names are matched case-insensitively, as Neo4j compares database names: spec.name may contain capitals, while SHOW DATABASES lists the database lower-cased.

name: Reconcile Neo4jReplicaDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves clusterRef, checks the version gate for cross-cluster replicas, then OBSERVES the live database's type (GetDatabaseInfo, which matches the name ignoring case) before dispatching on source.mode to create (backup or network), reporting, or terminally marking it promoted. While the database is still a replica it publishes the lag SHOW DATABASES reports (a transaction count) as neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions{namespace,cluster_name,replica,database,k8s_cluster}, and removes that series whenever it cannot vouch for it: when the CR is deleted, found gone, or promoted, when the database has vanished from the server, and when the downstream cluster is missing, not Ready or too old for replicas, the Neo4j client cannot connect, the database lookup fails, or the spec fails validation. The next successful observation sets the gauge again. The Neo4j client is obtained through an injectable factory (replicaNeo4jClient) so these branches are testable without a Bolt server. The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it (operations.md id 150).

name: Create Replica Database From Backup
description: Calls CreateReplicaDatabaseFromBackup with the upstream database, pull/seed URI, and optional topology when the target database does not yet exist (source.mode: backup). pullURI is either set directly or resolved by sf-resolve-upstream-backup-ref from source.upstreamBackupRef. Before an s3:// seed it checks that the downstream servers carry AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, read from spec.env, the live server container's env, and every variable an envFrom source supplies (spec.extraEnvFrom and the live container's envFrom, with the source's prefix); a source it cannot read, or a cloud workload identity, leaves the check to the server. A missing region leaves the replica Pending with one ev-replica-object-store-env-missing, and it carries on by itself once the servers have the region (knowledge operations.md id 145).

name: Detect Out-Of-Band Promotion
description: markPromoted() records the terminal Promoted phase the moment the live database's `type` column is observed to no longer be replica, whether caused by this operator's own Neo4jReplicaPromotion or an external actor. Removes the replica's neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions series, since a promoted database no longer replicates.

name: Drop Replica Database On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() re-checks the live database type and only issues DROP DATABASE while it is still type=replica; a promoted database is retained instead. Removes the replica's neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions series whatever the outcome.

name: Promote Replica Database
description: Reconcile() runs CHECK (live type=replica) -> PROMOTE (PromoteReplicaDatabase) -> CHECK (type no longer replica) -> RECORD, so a crash between the call and the status write is recovered as an idempotent success rather than a repeat promote. The terminal Completed/Failed phase latches: the first write that persists it increments neo4j_operator_replica_promotions_total{namespace,cluster_name,result,k8s_cluster} exactly once (result=success or failure) and later or stale reconciles count nothing; a successful promotion also removes the replica's lag series.

name: Reconcile Neo4jBackup
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec (including replication-source chain rules), resolves the target cluster/standalone, checks readiness/suspend, runs sharded preflight, and branches to the scheduled or one-time backup path. A one-time backup that is Completed or Failed returns before the target lookup, so a restarting target cannot reopen it; when the cached copy is not terminal the phase is read through the uncached APIReader (oneTimeBackupDone), so a pass on a copy from before the Completed write cannot start a second Job and write Failed over Completed (backup-restore.md Rule 113). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned a cloud identity's autoCreate.enabled: false into true and re-spelled resource quantities (operations.md id 150). A spec.chainFromBackup parent must name the same target; a database name matches it in any case (validateChainParent; knowledge operations.md id 146).

name: Create One-Time Backup Job
description: createBackupJob() creates exactly one Kubernetes Job per Neo4jBackup CR running `neo4j-admin database backup` (invariant: Job-per-CR, never a long-running backup pod/StatefulSet). With options.splitArchivePartSize on a 2026.09+ target it adds --split-archive-part-size=<bytes>; on an older target the Job is refused with a message naming the field. With backupType AUTO (the default) a shardedDatabase-scoped backup on a PVC passes --type=FULL (effectiveBackupType): only full shard backups can seed a sharded database from a PVC. A shardedDatabase-scoped backup names its shards with the patterns "<name>-g*" "<name>-p*", the logical name lower-cased (shardedBackupPatterns), so a database that only begins with the name — a copy restored as ProductsCopy — is neither backed up nor a reason to refuse the backup (backup-restore.md Rule 48).

name: Create Scheduled Backup CronJob
description: createBackupCronJob() creates/updates one CronJob per Neo4jBackup CR with spec.schedule set; each firing spawns its own child Job (still Job-per-run, never a persistent backup pod). With backupType AUTO (the default) a shardedDatabase-scoped backup on a PVC passes --type=FULL (effectiveBackupType): only full shard backups can seed a sharded database from a PVC. The scheduled path emits BackupScheduled only when the status write changes the phase or message (which names the CronJob and its schedule), not on every reconcile. Sharded backups use the same per-shard patterns as the one-time Job (backup-restore.md Rule 48).

name: Record Backup Run Outcome
description: recordOneShotBackupRun() / reconcileScheduledHistory() observe a completed Job's conditions, parse its pod log, and append a BackupRun to status.history, deferring finalization until restore-critical artifact filenames are captured — for at most artifactCaptureGrace (5 minutes) after the Job finished, not until the Job's TTL (backup-restore.md Rule 174) — including each artifact's FULL/DIFF type (status.history[].artifactType, databaseArtifacts[].type, shardArtifacts[].type), warning when a sharded run on a PVC wrote a differential shard. Expected shard names are the sharded database's spec.name lower-cased and are matched against the log ignoring case, as neo4j-admin writes them (backup-restore.md Rule 53). BackupCompleted and the Job-failed BackupFailed are emitted from the status write that enters the phase. updateBackupStatus stamps lastRunTime/lastSuccessTime when the backup enters Running/Completed and sends nothing when the status would not change (knowledge operations.md id 122).

name: Parse Backup Pod Log
description: neo4jbackup_log_parser.go's regex-based parsers extract per-shard/per-database .backup filenames, sizes, whether each artifact is FULL or DIFF (from neo4j-admin's 'full/differential backup of database' lines; an AUTO run that fell back to a full is FULL), and neo4j-admin backup validate results from a completed backup pod's stdout. A database named in spec is matched against the log ignoring case. Per-shard names from the log are merged into the expected shard list ignoring case (mergeShardArtifactsFromLog).

name: Cleanup Backup Artifacts
description: cleanupBackupArtifacts() runs an alpine-based cleanup Job (deterministic UID-derived name) enforcing spec.retention (maxCount/maxAge) against a PVC-backed chain directory; cloud storage retention is delegated to bucket lifecycle rules. Counts *.backup artifacts but deletes each one together with its split-archive parts (x.backup.*).

name: Reconcile Neo4jRestore
description: Main reconcile loop: resolves the target, checks terminal phases and version compatibility, and either polls in-flight progress or starts a fresh restore attempt. The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned a cloud identity's autoCreate.enabled: false into true; its own bookkeeping annotations (cypher-restore-issued, restore-pre-hooks-ran, point-in-time-path, seed-proxy-wait-started, ...) and the restore-in-progress annotation on a standalone target are merge patches too (operations.md id 150).

name: Start Restore
description: startRestore() validates the request, pins the resolved backup source onto status, and routes it: online (Cypher recreate/create with a seedURI, or the all-databases loop) for every cluster and for most standalone restores; the offline neo4j-admin Job (stopping the instance first when spec.stopCluster is set) only for a standalone restore that cannot be seeded online — point-in-time, a source.type storage path, cloud storage by pod identity, or a Job restore already holding the instance (rule 108). The offline path emits a RestoreStarted event naming the reason once its checks have passed (existence check, pre-restore hooks, and the stop or, with stopCluster false, the refusal of a running standalone), never for a restore it then refuses; with stopCluster true it is announced at the stop, which marks the standalone as this restore's; with stopCluster false, where nothing marks it, it is announced with the Job's start and says the standalone is already stopped, so a restore that waits in Pending after its checks does not announce twice. "Restore job … started" is emitted when the status write that makes the restore Running changed it, so a pass on a stale copy that finds the Job (AlreadyExists) announces nothing (knowledge operations.md id 145). With source.pointInTime it pins the earliest run that started at or after it (restoreRunIndex) and decides the point-in-time path before routing.

name: Route Restore Online or Offline
description: standaloneOfflineReason() / restoreRunsOffline() / restoreOnJobPath() (restore_target.go) decide, from the pinned status.resolvedSource, whether a restore runs online or takes the offline neo4j-admin Job: a cluster never takes the Job; a standalone does only for point-in-time, source.type storage, an unrecorded artifact, cloud storage with no credentialsSecretRef, or a Job restore that already holds its neo4j.com/restore-in-progress marker. The reason is reported in the refusal and the RestoreStarted event (rule 108). A standalone with spec.podServiceAccountAnnotations restores from cloud storage without a credentialsSecretRef online; a restore stays on the path it started on (restore-in-progress marker → Job, cypher-restore-issued or databaseResults → online). A restore with source.pointInTime runs online only as recorded once per attempt by decidePointInTimePath() in the neo4j.com/point-in-time-path annotation (CalVer, cloud storage, a covering run, a database that does not exist); a cluster that cannot fails with the reason.

name: Create Offline Standalone Restore Job
description: createRestoreJob() builds and creates the offline `neo4j-admin database restore` Job used only for a Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone restore that cannot run online (rule 108: point-in-time, a source.type storage path, cloud storage by pod identity) (neo4j-admin restore --overwrite-destination is documented as unsafe on clusters). --from-path names the exact artifact whenever it is known (backupPath ending in .backup, or the pinned snapshot's recorded file or per-database entry for the source database) — the only form neo4j-admin restores under a different name; otherwise it globs the source database's newest file (PVC) — `<database>-<yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH-mm-ss>.backup` with the name lower-cased, as neo4j-admin writes it, so a capitalised spec.database finds its artifacts and another database whose name begins with it is never taken (latestArtifactSubstitution; knowledge operations.md id 146) — or passes the cloud directory (same name only).

name: Online Cypher Restore
description: startClusterCypherRestore() restores one database online against the running DBMS — on a cluster and on a standalone (rule 108): dbms.[cluster.]recreateDatabase with a seedURI over an existing database (DatabaseExists, matching the name ignoring case), CREATE DATABASE … OPTIONS {seedURI} for a new one, then polls SHOW DATABASE until every allocation is online. Target-specific plumbing (StatefulSet name, pod labels for the seed proxy's NetworkPolicy, the CR that carries seed spec.env/extraEnvFrom) comes from restoreTarget. A PVC differential is merged by the seed proxy first (the proxy serves one file over HTTP; Neo4j refuses a DIFF without its chain); it runs pre-restore hooks before issuing and post-restore hooks once online; never a Job on cluster targets. Into a standalone by pod identity, awaitSeedIdentity() holds the seed until the pod runs under its identity ServiceAccount. A point-in-time restore creates the database with seedRestoreUntil (CreateDatabaseWithSeedURIUntil) and never recreates an existing one. When the target's server pods lack the cloud seed credentials or endpoint and the target is not opted in, awaitSeedConfig() holds the restore Pending (before any hook or database action) and it carries on once they are there; SeedEndpointNotProjected is announced when transitionRestoreStatus's write changed the phase or message, not from the pass's own copy. What a restore writes into that CR (spec.env, spec.extraEnvFrom, annotations) is a merge patch of those fields (updateTargetSpec; operations.md id 150).

name: All-Databases Restore Loop
description: startAllDatabasesRestore() drives one per-database CREATE/recreate-with-seedURI action per reconcile pass from the resolved backup's per-database artifact map, on clusters and standalones, tracking progress in status.databaseResults; runs pre-restore hooks once per attempt (neo4j.com/restore-pre-hooks-ran) and post-restore hooks before Completed, has the seed proxy merge each database's PVC chain that is not recorded as FULL, and stamps status.completionTime. Property-sharded families are excluded and must restore via their own Neo4jShardedDatabase CR. Into a standalone by pod identity, awaitSeedIdentity() holds the seed until the pod runs under its identity ServiceAccount. Missing cloud seed credentials or endpoint hold it Pending (awaitSeedConfig()) before the first database is seeded, and it carries on once they are there. Each database's RestoreStarted and RestoreSeedProgress go through ProgressRecorder (source neo4j-restore-progress), an event budget of its own; RestoreSeedProgress is announced when a database's progress changes and every 10 minutes while it does not (seedProgressEvents). The outcome is one RestoreCompleted or RestoreFailed from the status write that changed the phase (finishAllDatabasesRestore), which the per-database events cannot crowd out of the restore's budget (knowledge operations.md id 166). The Neo4j client is reached through allDatabasesRestoreClient so a test can script it.

name: Handle Restore Success
description: handleRestoreSuccess() restarts a stopped cluster, registers/starts the restored database(s) (or all restored databases), runs post-restore hooks, and forces a cross-server recreate-from-seed so every server converges on the restored server-0 data.

name: Resolve Cluster Reference
description: ResolveClusterRef() looks up a clusterRef, trying Neo4jEnterpriseCluster first and falling back to Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone of the same name, returning a ResolvedTarget with IsReady()/NewClient() helpers. IsReady() accepts a cluster whose phase is Ready or Degraded, or whose Ready condition is True (clusterAcceptsWork), so dependents keep working against a cluster that is serving with a majority of its servers.

name: Resolve Backup Reference
description: ResolveBackupRef() dereferences a Neo4jBackup CR name into a concrete StorageLocation and the BackupsPath of its most recent Succeeded run, returning a wrapped ErrBackupNotReady when no Succeeded run exists yet.

name: Reconcile Neo4jUser
description: Drives a Neo4jUser to its desired state each loop: validates the spec (routing a not-yet-applied password Secret to Pending, not Failed), resolves the clusterRef target, creates or ALTERs the Neo4j user over Bolt (the home database compared with SHOW USERS ignoring case), diffs granted vs. desired roles and issues GRANT/REVOKE ROLE, then records RolesSynced/PasswordSynced conditions and the Ready phase. A desired role counts as existing when it is built in, granted, a Neo4jRole CR or listed by SHOW ROLES (a role created in Neo4j directly), so such a role is granted (missingRoles; operations.md id 17). While the target is not Ready a Ready user stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True (waitForTarget), and UserReady is announced from the write that enters Ready (operations.md id 158). A retried DROP USER on deletion is written to status and announced once (id 145). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it (operations.md id 150). CR names in spec.roles that resolve to another Neo4j role name are recorded in the RoleNamesResolved condition (reportResolvedRoles), and RolesResolved is emitted only when that mapping appears or changes (operations.md id 136). Its Neo4j calls go through the userNeo4jClient seam, which tests script. A connection failure to a target that reads Ready but cannot be reached — at connect or mid-pass — is the rest of the target's outage: the same wait with reason ClusterUnreachable, logged at info, retried on the fixed interval without an error, reported as ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes (unreachable; operations.md id 172). The password's change token is recorded by a status write right after the statement that applied it (passwordApplied), which announces PasswordRotated, so a pass a failing grant stops does not send the same ALTER again (operations.md id 15).

name: Reconcile Neo4jRole
description: Drives a Neo4jRole to its desired state each loop: validates the spec, creates the role if absent (refusing built-ins without adoptBuiltin), normalises spec.privileges to Neo4j's stored rendering (sf-normalise-role-privileges) and diffs that against live SHOW ROLE PRIVILEGES AS COMMANDS output, applies missing GRANT/DENY statements verbatim, and derives REVOKE statements textually for privileges no longer desired (never revoking immutable ones). Before applying, it resolves each missing grant's database names against SHOW DATABASES and aliases (case-insensitively) and skips grants naming a database that does not exist, reporting them via PrivilegesResolve=False instead of failing the reconcile; they apply once the database exists. The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned spec.enforcePrivileges: false into true, so privileges added outside the spec were revoked (operations.md id 150). While the target is not Ready a Ready role stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True (waitForTarget), and RoleReady is announced from the write that enters Ready (reportReady; operations.md id 158). A missing built-in role, and a learn-mode status write the API server will not keep, are retried on the fixed interval, not left unrequeued or to error backoff (operations.md id 95). A retried DROP ROLE on deletion is written to status and announced once (id 145). Database names in its warnings are de-duplicated ignoring case (distinctPrivilegeTargets; id 146). A connection failure to a target that reads Ready but cannot be reached — at connect or mid-pass — is the rest of the target's outage: the same wait with reason ClusterUnreachable, logged at info, retried on the fixed interval without an error, reported as ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes (unreachable; operations.md id 172).

name: Render Privilege Rules
description: rolePrivilegeStatements() renders each spec.privilegeRules entry with neo4j.RenderPrivilegeRule (backtick-escaped names, one segment) and appends it to spec.privileges, so every downstream path — normalisation, learn mode, resolve reporting, the dropped-database warning — sees one desired set. A Neo4jDatabase watch re-queues roles naming that database (internal/controller/neo4jrole_rules.go).

name: Reconcile Neo4jRoleBinding
description: Drives a Neo4jRoleBinding to its desired state each loop: verifies the target Neo4j user already exists (bindings never create/drop users), resolves Neo4jRole CR names to Neo4j role names, and diffs/grants/revokes role membership — non-exclusive by default, but always revoking roles this binding previously granted that were removed from spec.roles. A role created in Neo4j directly (SHOW ROLES) counts as existing and is granted (missingRoles; operations.md id 17). While the target is not Ready a Ready binding stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True, and BindingCreated / BindingUpdated are announced from the write that records the change (operations.md id 158). A retried revoke on deletion is written to status and announced once (id 145). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it (operations.md id 150). The resolved CR-name mapping is recorded in the RoleNamesResolved condition (reportResolvedRoles), and RolesResolved is emitted only when it appears or changes (operations.md id 136). Its Neo4j calls go through the roleBindingNeo4jClient seam, which tests script. A connection failure to a target that reads Ready but cannot be reached — at connect or mid-pass — is the rest of the target's outage: the same wait with reason ClusterUnreachable, logged at info, retried on the fixed interval without an error, reported as ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes (unreachable; operations.md id 172).

name: Reconcile Neo4jAuthRule
description: Drives a Neo4jAuthRule to its desired state each loop: gates on the cluster running Neo4j 2026.03+ and configuring an OIDC authorization provider, then CREATE OR REPLACEs the rule's condition/enabled flag (which clears prior grants) and re-grants the desired role set via GRANT/REVOKE ROLES ... TO/FROM AUTH RULE. The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned spec.enforceRoles: false into true (operations.md id 150). While the target is not Ready a Ready rule stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True (operations.md id 158), and a retried DROP AUTH RULE on deletion is written to status and announced once (id 145). A connection failure to a target that reads Ready but cannot be reached — at connect or mid-pass — is the rest of the target's outage: the same wait with reason ClusterUnreachable, logged at info, retried on the fixed interval without an error, reported as ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes (unreachable; operations.md id 172).

name: Create Neo4j user
description: CreateUserAdvanced issues CREATE USER `name` IF NOT EXISTS with staged SET PASSWORD/SET STATUS/SET HOME DATABASE/SET AUTH clauses against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Alter Neo4j user
description: AlterUser issues ALTER USER with REMOVE clauses ordered before SET clauses (password, password-change-required, suspended status, home database, external auth providers) against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Drop Neo4j user
description: DropUserIfExists issues DROP USER `name` IF EXISTS against the system database, making user removal idempotent (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Grant role to user
description: GrantRoleToUser issues GRANT ROLE `role` TO `user` against the system database (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Revoke role from user
description: RevokeRoleFromUser issues REVOKE ROLE `role` FROM `user` against the system database (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Create Neo4j role
description: CreateRoleAdvanced issues CREATE ROLE `name` [IF NOT EXISTS] [AS COPY OF `copyOf`] against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Drop Neo4j role
description: DropRoleIfExists issues DROP ROLE `name` IF EXISTS against the system database; built-in roles are never dropped by any caller (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Apply privilege statement
description: ExecutePrivilegeStatement runs the role's original (non-canonicalised) GRANT/DENY privilege statement text as auto-commit Cypher against the system database, with bounded retry on transient GQLSTATUS 25N11 conflicting-transaction errors (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Revoke privilege statement
description: Runs a REVOKE statement derived textually from the role's currently-applied GRANT/DENY command via DerivePrivilegeRevoke (internal/neo4j/privileges.go) through ExecutePrivilegeStatement — REVOKEs are never accepted directly from Neo4jRole.spec.privileges, and immutable privileges are skipped rather than attempted.

name: Show role privileges
description: ShowRolePrivileges runs SHOW ROLE `name` PRIVILEGES AS COMMANDS YIELD command, immutable (falling back to a legacy projection without immutable on older Neo4j) to read a role's currently-applied privilege set from the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Create or replace auth rule
description: CreateOrReplaceAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 CREATE OR REPLACE AUTH RULE `name` SET CONDITION <expr> SET ENABLED true|false against the system database, subsuming ALTER semantics by replacing the rule outright (and clearing its prior role grants) (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Grant roles to auth rule
description: GrantRolesToAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 GRANT ROLES r1, r2, ... TO AUTH RULE `name` against the system database (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Revoke roles from auth rule
description: RevokeRolesFromAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 REVOKE ROLES r1, r2, ... FROM AUTH RULE `name` against the system database (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Drop auth rule
description: DropAuthRuleIfExists issues CYPHER 25 DROP AUTH RULE `name` IF EXISTS against the system database during Neo4jAuthRule deletion cleanup (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Validate Neo4jUser spec
description: UserValidator.Validate enforces the Neo4j username shape/length, requires at least one auth provider (passwordSecretRef or externalAuth), rejects the reserved 'system' username and the 'native' externalAuth provider, WARNS (without rejecting) when the username is the default bootstrap admin 'neo4j' because managing it rewrites the credential the operator itself authenticates with, and reports a not-yet-applied password Secret as a transient Pending gap rather than a Failed error (internal/validation/user_validator.go).

name: Validate Neo4jRole spec
description: RoleValidator.Validate enforces the Neo4j role-name pattern, requires spec.adoptBuiltin=true to manage a built-in role name, requires every spec.privileges entry to start with GRANT/DENY and end with `TO <this role>`, and rejects property-based-access-control privileges that target a Neo4jShardedDatabase (internal/validation/role_validator.go).

name: Validate Neo4jRoleBinding spec
description: RoleBindingValidator.Validate enforces the shared username shape check, requires spec.roles to be non-empty with no blank entries, and warns (never errors) when PUBLIC is listed since it is implicit and always ignored (internal/validation/rolebinding_validator.go).

name: Validate Neo4jAuthRule spec
description: AuthRuleValidator.Validate enforces the auth-rule name pattern, requires spec.condition to be a pure expression free of DDL keywords (CREATE/DROP/ALTER/GRANT/DENY/REVOKE/SHOW/RENAME/semicolon) to block Cypher injection, and requires at least one entry in spec.grantedRoles (internal/validation/authrule_validator.go).

name: Validate spec.config
description: ConfigValidator.ValidateConfigMap, shared by the cluster and the standalone validator (and so by kubectl neo4j validate): refuses removed 4.x keys and families, the keys the operator manages itself (discovery, advertised addresses, topology, SSL policy, db.format), line breaks in values, and, for the settings in typedSettings whose type is identical on the 5.26 LTS and CalVer (memory, transaction log, checkpoints, timeouts, query logging, Bolt thread pool, routing, authentication), a value Neo4j would refuse at startup or one below a documented minimum, reported on spec.config[<key>] with the expected format and an example (ValidateSettingValues, internal/validation/setting_values.go; operations.md id 140). A cluster with property sharding enabled also has spec.propertySharding.config checked. The readers mirror Neo4j's own parsers (ByteUnit.parse, TimeUtil.parseTimeMillis, Integer/Long.parseLong, equalsIgnoreCase) and never refuse a spelling they do not model; unlisted settings, $(command) values and backslash escapes pass. The memory rules (heap plus page cache within the memory limit) read sizes with the same byte-size reader.

name: Reconcile AuraInstance
description: Top-level AuraInstanceReconciler.Reconcile loop: handles the paused annotation, then deletion (which resolves the credentials only to call Aura, operations.md id 157), then resolves credentials and the finalizer; a terminal create refusal already on status for the current generation stops the pass before Aura is called (refusalStands, id 156); dispatches to create/adopt, drift, tier-upgrade, pause/resume and deletion, then writes status.atProvider plus the Ready/Synced conditions. Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156). fail() writes phase Error with the Ready condition.

name: Create or adopt Aura instance
description: observeOrCreate: lists instances by name to adopt before creating (avoiding a duplicate paid instance), validates the type/region/cloudProvider combo against the project's instance_configurations, and creates via v1 CreateInstance or, when spec.multiDatabase is true, via v2beta1 CreateInstanceV2 (createMultiDatabaseInstance in aura_multidatabase.go). A 429, a 5xx or a transport failure of the list or the create is marked where the call failed (retryableAuraCall) and retried without a status write; everything else, the operator's own errors included, is recorded as CreateFailed (operations.md id 88).

name: Resize/patch Aura instance
description: reconcileDrift: PATCHes memory, storage, name, secondariesCount and cdcEnrichmentMode when they diverge from the observed instance, gated by the Update management policy.

name: Pause Aura instance
description: reconcilePauseResume: calls PauseInstance when spec.paused=true and the observed instance is running.

name: Resume Aura instance
description: reconcilePauseResume: calls ResumeInstance when spec.paused=false and the observed instance is paused.

name: Upgrade Aura instance tier
description: reconcileUpgrade: performs the single supported in-place tier upgrade (professional-db to business-critical) via UpgradeInstance when spec.type requests it; the CRD's CEL transition rule already rejects every other type change.

name: Delete/orphan Aura instance
description: handleDeletion: honours deletionPolicy before releasing the finalizer. Orphan, the default, leaves the cloud instance running and needs no credentials; Delete calls DeleteInstance unless deletionProtection is set, resolving the credentials only then. A Delete that cannot resolve them records CredentialsUnavailable and retries, and after finalizerDeletionGracePeriod (5 minutes) releases the finalizer with a Warning AuraInstanceOrphaned (operations.md id 157).

name: Reconcile AuraSnapshot
description: AuraSnapshotReconciler.Reconcile: requests a snapshot exactly once via CreateSnapshot, then polls GetSnapshot until Completed/Failed/Cancelled; the create response carries only snapshot_id so the initial phase is recorded as Pending rather than copying fields that are not yet present.

name: Reconcile AuraRestore
description: AuraRestoreReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the target AuraInstance and a snapshot (spec.snapshotId or an AuraSnapshot ref), waits for the instance to be Running, calls RestoreSnapshot, then drives Pending->Restoring->Completed/Failed and never re-fires once terminal.

name: Reconcile AuraDatabase
description: AuraDatabaseReconciler.Reconcile: resolves org/project/instance coordinates from the referenced AuraInstance (which must have been created with multiDatabase:true), refuses creation when the instance's probed multiDatabase verdict is explicitly false, and otherwise creates/adopts the database by the external-database-id annotation since the v2beta1 API returns no database names to adopt by. Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). The InstanceNotMultiDatabase refusal, once on status for the current generation and the same Aura instance ID, is not asked again; a transient failure of the list or the create is retried without a status write; AuraDatabaseReady is announced when the database becomes Ready (ids 88, 136, 156). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156).

name: Reconcile AuraDatabaseBackup
description: AuraDatabaseBackupReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the target database via spec.databaseRef, takes the backup exactly once via CreateDatabaseBackup, then polls GetDatabaseBackup, treating only Completed/Failed as terminal and never inferring completion from an empty just-scheduled status. Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). A 429, a 5xx, a transport failure or a 409 of the backup create is retried, not recorded as BackupFailed (id 88). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156).

name: Reconcile AuraDatabaseRestore
description: AuraDatabaseRestoreReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the database and backup (by spec.backupId or an AuraDatabaseBackup ref), persists a Submitting marker before calling RestoreDatabase (the destructive, non-idempotent call), and records Submitted (not Completed, since v2beta1 exposes no way to observe restore completion) or RestoreOutcomeUnknown if the process died mid-flight.

name: Reconcile Aura org/project member
description: AuraOrganizationMemberReconciler.Reconcile and its AuraProjectMemberReconciler counterpart find an existing Aura console user by email (ListOrgMembers/ListProjectMembers), update their org or project role when it drifts from spec.role, and remove membership on CR deletion; a project member with no project membership yet but an existing org membership is added via AddProjectMember rather than requiring a fresh invite.
